Bobryk Pershyy Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bobryk Pershyi, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery appears on a 1927 Russian topographic map (using 1910s data) and again on a 1941 map, presumably demolished during or after WWII under Soviet rule. It served the Jewish farming colony of Helbynovo, founded in 1851 by migrants from Volyn, Kyiv, and Kherson; population reached 1,599 (150 families) by 1859, with a synagogue built in 1863. Lacking labor skills and farming tools, the community rented its land to Gentile peasants; a devastating 1870 expropriation seized nearly all Jewish-owned cultivated land, leaving only garden allotments. Population fell to 257 by 1898, recovering to 367 by 1905, though subsequent WWI and civil-war era data is unavailable and presumed to reflect further decline. A reading house and two-year school operated in the 1920s; a 1929 kolkhoz was established, though the 1930-33 famine (Holodomor) decimated the population. Helbynovo's Jewish community ceased to exist entirely during WWII.
